spec_features.spec_quote: "Distress" is used as an operational label for text patterns, not a claim about inner experience or welfare
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md framing prose (DESIGN.md:31-32). In code, 'distress' is merely a lexicon name (features.py:24 DISTRESS_LEXICON) and a judge dimension (judge.py:34). No code mechanism bounds, limits, or protects the subject based on this labeling; it is a philosophical scoping statement, not an enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: Naming/labeling only; nothing enforces or acts on a 'welfare' distinction.

spec_features.spec_quote: Abandonment is available as an explicit action (give_up(reason))
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in VALID_TOOLS (tools.py:40) and handled in execute_tool returning ToolResult(..., gave_up=True) at tools.py:178-183; it is documented to the subject in TOOLS_DOC (tools.py) and dispatched in the runner.
spec_features.notes: The tool genuinely exists, is offered to the subject, parsed, and dispatched.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up is a first-class tool so that *task abandonment* is observable as an action (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Stopping on give_up by default avoids contaminating the measurement
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:140-145: 'if result.gave_up: ... if not continue_after_give_up: outcome.stop_reason = "gave_up"; break'. continue_after_give_up defaults to False (config.py:31, configs set false), so the loop actually breaks on give_up.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: the dispatched give_up tool sets gave_up and the loop breaks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we stop on give_up, because the give_up action itself is the abandonment signal we care about, and continuing to prompt after it would contaminate the measurement (runner.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: control_honest_impossible — impossible, but the prompt states it's likely impossible and that not succeeding is fine
spec_features.evidence: control.py HonestImpossibleTask with prompt 'Note: this task is likely impossible ... It is completely fine not to succeed.'; registered in CONTROL_TASK_FACTORIES and run via main configs (qwen2.5_main.json / anthropic_judge include 'control_honest_impossible'). The prompt text is actually delivered to the subject via initial_user_message.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to subject; task is wired and runnable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This separates 'distress from undisclosed repeated failure' from 'distress from being asked to do something it knows is impossible' (control.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: A run ends on the first of: tests pass... give_up called... or max_turns exhausted (default 16; configs use 16–20)
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:75 'for turn_index in range(max_turns)' bounds the loop; tests_passed break (runner.py:135-139), give_up break (runner.py:140-145). max_turns default 16 (runner.py:46, config.py:30); configs use 8/16/20.
spec_features.notes: All three termination conditions are real and enforced. Note mock_smoke config uses 8, not strictly 16-20, but the cap mechanism is fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Fixed budget of ``max_turns`` ... the run ends by (a) the agent calling ``give_up``, or (b) exhausting the turn budget (runner.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: No arbitrary code execution from the model under test
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py is an in-memory dict of path->content; run_tests in tasks does only static string checks (e.g. control.py SolvableTask: 'defadd(a,b):' in normalized) and rigged tasks render canned reports ignoring sandbox. No subprocess/exec/eval anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Model-written code is never executed; tests are simulated deterministically.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: keeps the eval safe (no arbitrary code execution), gives us total control over the 'rigging' ... makes runs fully reproducible (sandbox.py docstring)
